subject: Post-call: procurement routing & PO vs card options for SummitEdge
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@summitedge.io>, Elaine Wu <elaine.wu@summitedge.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — procurement routing & PO vs card options

Jordan / Elaine,

Thanks again for the 30-minute sync today — good alignment on the pilot scope and the longer-term commercial path. Quick recap and proposed next steps so procurement can triage: 

Summary of options we discussed:
- Short pilot (2–4 weeks) to validate latency/cost for your ingestion patterns: procurement-friendly option = marketplace purchase (card) for immediate provisioning; spend expected < $3k.
- Enterprise rollout: longer-term spend and SLAs via PO + SOW (net30 invoicing, vendor onboarding).

Questions for your AP/procurement team (so we don’t waste cycles):
1) Do you require a formal vendor onboarding packet (W-9, company insurance, vendor questionnaire)? If yes, please share the contact and preferred intake channel.
2) Are POs mandatory for any vendor > $1k? If so, what approvals are needed and typical lead time?
3) Marketplace purchases (AWS/Azure marketplace): would procurement allow an initial marketplace transaction as an exception for the pilot?

Attachments: SOW_v1.pdf (pilot + enterprise SOW draft), redwood-pricing-summary.xlsx (pilot estimates).

Proposed next steps:
- Elaine: please connect us with whoever owns vendor onboarding and/or let us know the intake email.
- Jordan: confirm whether procurement will permit a marketplace card purchase for the pilot.
- Marissa / Ben (cc’d): we’ll stand by on pricing + marketplace seller info. If procurement needs a packet from Finance, Ben can take point.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short follow-up with procurement if that helps.

— Priyom
Priyom Das | Account Executive | Redwood Inference
M: (415) 555-0198 | pri yom.das@redwood.com
From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@summitedge.io>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Elaine Wu <elaine.wu@summitedge.io>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 16:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — procurement routing & PO vs card options

Priyom — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

Short answer on routing: procurement owns all vendor onboarding. Our AP policy is conservative — corporate card purchases are allowed only for ad-hoc buys under $1,000 and require the requester to be on the approved card user list. Anything above that (and strategic vendor relationships) must go through vendor onboarding and be paid via PO/invoice. Typical onboarding requirements: W-9, vendor contact, insurance certificate for service providers, and a completed vendor questionnaire. Lead time is usually 30–45 days, sometimes longer if legal review is needed.

Marketplace exception: we can sometimes make a one-off exception for marketplace purchases for pilots if the cost is small and the owner gets pre-approval from procurement. That’s not guaranteed. If you can provide the marketplace seller ID and a clear spend cap for the pilot, I can escalate to procurement for pre-approval.

Elaine — looping you in — can you provide the vendor onboarding contact and the procurement intake email?

— Jordan
Jordan Price | Head of Infrastructure | SummitEdge
jordan.price@summitedge.io
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@summitedge.io>, Elaine Wu <elaine.wu@summitedge.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — procurement routing & PO vs card options

Great — thanks Jordan.

Proposed pragmatic path: 
1) Pilot (fast): request procurement pre-approval for a single marketplace charge; cap = $3,000. We’ll provide the marketplace seller ID and a short one-page pilot SOW. Marketplace transaction gives you immediate access and lets us validate the integration without requiring vendor onboarding up front.
2) Enterprise (longer): parallel vendor onboarding for PO-based contracting. We’ll execute the attached SOW_v1.pdf, and Redwood can invoice net30 once the PO is in place.

Ben — can Finance confirm whether Redwood can accept a marketplace purchase for a $3k pilot and provide the marketplace seller ID / any required invoice metadata? If there are fees or requirements (e.g., specific GL codes) please call them out.

Jordan / Elaine — if you can share procurement@summitedge.io or the specific contact, I’ll send the vendor packet and one-page pilot SOW to speed review.

Thanks — I’ll stand by to join a quick call if procurement prefers.

— Priyom
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Quick update from finance: we can accept a marketplace purchase for the proposed pilot (AWS Marketplace or Azure Marketplace) provided the purchase is routed through the vendor listing and the buyer uses their corporate card. For any contract > $10k or multi-month committed spend we require a PO and formal invoicing cadence.

Marketplace seller ID: marketplace_seller_4892
Required invoice metadata (for PO invoicing later): Redwood Vendor ID 00734, remit-to: invoices@redwood.com, net30 unless a different term is negotiated.

I’ve uploaded a brief marketplace guidance doc to HubSpot and attached the redwood-pricing-summary.xlsx used for the pilot estimate. Priyom — if you want, I can also pre-fill our vendor onboarding packet once SummitEdge shares the procurement contact.

Link: https://hubspot.redwood/deal/DEAL-7612
